title: Metabolic Support of Excised, Living Brain Tissues During Magnetic Resonance Microscopy Acquisition
protocol: Make fresh artificial cerebrospinal fluid (aCSF).
Measure out 1,500 mL of water purified by double distillation or reverse osmosis into a 4 L flask.
Place a magnetic stir bar in the flask and agitate using a stir plate.

Dissolve 14.03 g sodium chloride, 4.37 g sodium bicarbonate, 0.41 g monobasic potassium phosphate, 0.69 g magnesium sulfate heptahydrate, 0.59 g calcium chloride dihydrate, and 0.45 g potassium chloride into the purified water.
Dissolve 3.6 g glucose in the solution.
Mix thoroughly until all salts have dissolved.
Adjust volume to 2 L using additional purified water.
Test the osmolality of the aCSF using a freezing point depression osmometer.
Adjust the aCSF to 300 mOsm/kg by adding sorbitol.
Add 324 mg of sorbitol to 2 L of 299 mOsm/kg aCSF perfusate.
Set up the aCSF perfusion system.
Equilibrate aCSF to ambient temperature (~23 °C) while gassing with 95% carbogen (95% O2, 5% CO2; 1/16 L/min).
Confirm that the pH of the aCSF is in the physiological range (7.3 - 7.4).
Continue to bubble gas directly into the perfusate reservoir throughout the experiment.
Prime the perfusion lines by submerging the inlet tube connected to the peristaltic micro-pump into the prepared aCSF (300 mOsm, pH 7.3 - 7.4, continuously gassed).
Pass the oxygenator device and perfusion lines through the magnet bore and gradient coil stack.
Hang the oxygenator above a beaker to catch any aCSF effluent.
Invert the empty, in-line bubble trap so that aCSF displaces the air inside.
Connect the oxygenator's gas port to a carbogen source and set a flow rate of 1/16L/min.
Dip the exhaust port on top of the oxygenator into water to confirm carbogen is flowing over the membrane.
Purge visible gas bubbles from the inflow lines by manual agitation once aCSF is detected dripping from the perfusion chamber.
Submerge the oxygen electrode in the aCSF flowing from the perfusion chamber to confirm correct operation.
Place a rat (125 - 150 g) into the induction chamber of an anesthesia machine.
Expose the rat to 4% isoflurane in an oxygen carrier gas at a rate of 1 L/min for 4 min.
Remove the unconscious rat from the anesthesia chamber.
Perform a righting reflex test by placing the rat in the supine position and checking for any movements indicative that the animal is turning onto its stomach.
Perform an eye-blink reflexive test by touching the open eye of the animal using a cotton swab and checking for lid closure or muscle twitching.
Perform a limb-withdraw reflex test by pinching the skin between the toes of the rat's outstretched back leg and checking for flexion of the leg.
If any reflex tests elicit a response, return the rat immediately to the anesthesia chamber.
Allow an additional 2 min of exposure to 4% isoflurane in the event that reflexive tests show positive responses.
Repeat all three reflexive tests over entirely after each 2 min anesthesia exposure until no responses are observed.
Euthanize the rat via guillotine decapitation once a complete lack of response to all three reflexive tests has been confirmed.
Remove rat brain by gross dissection.
Place the head in the prone position.
Cut rostrally through the skin from the back of the neck to the nose with scissors to expose the skull.
Remove soft tissues from the surface of the skull with a blunt probe.
Use rongeurs to remove the occipital, parietal, and frontal bones of the cranium starting from the caudal end.
Cut along the longitudinal fissure with micro scissors and peel back the dura layer from both hemispheres.
Turn the head to the supine position and sever the cranial nerves on the ventral side to remove the brain from the skull.
Isolate the central portion containing the hippocampus by removing all tissues caudal to the transverse fissure and rostral to the fimbria.
Make two cuts along the transverse plane with a straight-edged razor.
Affix the brain's caudal-most plane to the center of a vibratome cutting bath using cyanoacrylate glue.
Add ice-cold, carbogen-bubbled aCSF to the vibratome cutting bath and place the nylon retention hardware inside.
Cut 300 μm thick slices to obtain 3 to 4 usable slice preparations per hemisphere (6 to 8 total).
Isolate a hippocampus or cortical section from one hemisphere.
Trim the slice so that it fits within the microcoil's 5 mm diameter tissue well.
Fill the microcoil's tissue chamber with oxygenated aCSF using a transfer pipette.
Position the region of interest over the microcoil using a dissecting scope.
Insert the tissue retention device to retain sample position throughout the experiment.
Affix the modified microcoil assembly in a table clamp.
Attach the acetal support peg into the hole on top of the coil for the oxygenator.
Place the perfusion chamber over the microcoil's tissue well and secure with a miniature cable tie.
Trim excess length from the cable tie using wire cutters.
Confirm that perfusate exits through the outflow lines without leakage around the silicone seal.
Attach the microcoil and oxygenator assembly to the top of the imaging probe body.
Slide the gradient stack over the assembly.
Seat the gradient on top of the probe.
Place the probe body in close proximity to the spectrometer bore opening at the bottom of the magnet.
Retract the excess length of perfusion lines through the bore opening at the top of the magnet.
Advance the probe body into the magnet bore at the base while simultaneously removing more slack from the perfusion lines from the top of the bore.
Thread the two securing screws at the base of the probe into the corresponding slots of the shim stack.
Check that perfusate flow has recommenced prior to attempting reinsertion if no perfusate is seen exiting the return line into the waste reservoir.
Attach the inflow and outflow water lines from the gradient chiller.
Turn on the pump for the gradient chiller and confirm the water temperature setting is 19 °C.
Attach the air hose from the air chiller unit to the probe body using a hose clamp.
Turn the flow knob on the air chiller unit to the "1" position.
Attach the thermocouple wire to the probe body.
Attach the coaxial cable from the preamp to the RF input/output on the probe body's proton (H) channel.
Attach the power cable from the gradient amplifiers to the probe body.
Inside the RF cabinet, turn on the power to the B0 compensation unit.
Turn on the power to all three gradient amplifiers (x,y,z).
Turn on the power to the master unit.
Set the intended bore temperature using the variable temperature adjustment module at the console.
Match and tune the RF circuit by adjusting the variable capacitors within the probe.
Adjust the current settings for the spectrometer's shim coils to maximize magnetic field homogeneity at the sample.
Collect pilot images to determine the spatial position of the sample within the magnet bore.
Use typical parameters for a two-dimensional gradient echo (TR/TE = 100/4 ms, averages = 1, pulse angle = 30°, time = 6 sec, matrix = 64 x 64, field of view = 0.3 x 0.3 cm, resolution = 47 x 47 μm).
Collect diffusion-weighted pilots to confirm proper scan geometry and tissue position.

Use typical parameters for a two-dimensional diffusion-weighted pilot scan: TR/TE = 2000/11.6 ms, time = 4.3 min, Δ = 6 ms, δ = 1 ms, averages = 1, b = 1200 s/mm² (effective b = 1860 s/mm²), matrix = 64 x 64, field of view = 0.2 x 0.2 cm, resolution = 31 μm.
Collect a diffusion-weighted time series to determine the stability characteristics of the acute slice preparation.

Use typical parameters for a two-dimensional diffusion-weighted image: TR/TE = 2000/11.6 ms, time = 1.5 h, Δ = 6 ms, δ = 1 ms, averages = 42, b = 1200 s/mm², matrix = 64 x 64, field of view = 0.2 x 0.2 cm, resolution = 31 μm.
Note: Characterizing stability in a given system may vary depending on the MR contrast employed, physical perturbation studied, and MR signal change per unit time resulting from said perturbation.
